authorities.locator: 2024 U.S. Code edition, codification PDF pages 337-338; subsections (a)(1) and (b)(4)(A)
authorities.proposition: Judicial review of a final removal order proceeds under the specified review scheme; the reviewing court may not order additional evidence under 28 U.S.C. § 2347(c) and decides the petition only on the administrative record on which the order was based.

authorities.locator: 2024 U.S. Code edition, codification PDF page 338; subsection (b)(4)(B)
authorities.proposition: Administrative findings of fact are conclusive unless any reasonable adjudicator would be compelled to conclude to the contrary.

authorities.locator: 2024 U.S. Code edition, codification PDF page 338; subsection (b)(1)
authorities.proposition: A petition for review must be filed not later than 30 days after the date of the final order of removal.
An applicant for CAT withholding bears the burden to establish that the applicant is more likely than not to be tortured in the proposed country of removal.
All evidence relevant to possible future torture must be considered, including evidence of past torture, relocation, gross or mass rights violations, and other country conditions.
An applicant entitled to CAT protection but subject to the identified mandatory-denial provisions receives deferral of removal to the country where torture is more likely than not.

authorities.locator: 2025 annual edition, printed pages 1054-1055; subsections (a)(1) and (a)(7)
authorities.proposition: Torture includes qualifying severe intentional harm by, at the instigation of, or with consent or acquiescence of a public official acting officially; acquiescence requires awareness and breach of a duty to intervene, and awareness includes actual knowledge or willful blindness.

authorities.locator: Rule 16(a)-(b), Composition of the Record; Omissions From or Misstatements in the Record
authorities.proposition: The agency-review record consists of the agency order, findings or report, and agency pleadings, evidence, and proceedings; an omission or misstatement is corrected as directed by the court, and a supplemental record may be prepared and filed.

Section 1252(b)(1)'s 30-day deadline is a nonjurisdictional claims-processing rule; such a matter is ordinarily forfeited if not timely raised, and the Court did not dismiss where the Government chose not to press the filing ground.

authorities.locator: Part III, 915 F.3d at 974-977; official published PDF pages 7-10
authorities.proposition: CAT risk from all feared sources must be considered in the aggregate rather than as separate, divisible claims.

authorities.locator: Part IV and conclusion, 915 F.3d at 977-980; official published PDF pages 10-13
authorities.proposition: The agency may not arbitrarily ignore relevant, legally significant CAT evidence; failure to meaningfully engage the evidence hampers review and can require vacatur and remand.
